provenance.source_section: 10.2 If you hear an old word
provenance.note: A copy, with provenance. Re-derive and compare with `scripts/check-retired-vocabulary-table`; that check needs both repositories present and is not part of the pytest suite, because a guard that skips when its source is absent reads exactly like one that passed. Running it by hand is the decision rather than a gap waiting on automation (#684): automating it needs a standing credential for one private repository to read another, which is a permanent grant bought against a rare event in a codebase with a finite life. Re-run it when §10.2 changes; it exits 2, not 0, when it cannot read the spec.

revisions.this-revision: SPD-194, `h3tech-ai/synaptory-spec` 2026-09-07. The revision that ships section 10.2 in its current form. Section 10.2 writes this cell as "**This revision**", relative to itself, so it is named here instead. When the spec ships a later revision these rows become "Earlier revision" and the drift check fires.
revisions.earlier-revision: A revision before SPD-194; section 10.2 names it only as "Earlier revision". In this repository the same rename is recorded by docs/adrs/ADR-028-spq-cycle-vocabulary.md, which cites `SPD-173` for Slice -> Cycle, superseding `SPD-120`'s Increment.
